draft.title: Modulus and argument
card: A complex number z = a + bi is plotted on the Argand plane as the point (a, b). The horizontal axis is real and the vertical axis is imaginary.
|z| is the distance from the origin to the point. |z| = √(a² + b²).
Arg z is the angle from the positive real axis to the line joining the origin to the point. It is measured anticlockwise, and in this course it lies in the range −π < θ ≤ π.
Example: z = −1 + i. |z| = √(1 + 1) = √2. The point is in the second quadrant, on a line at 45° to the negative real axis, so Arg z = π − π/4 = 3π/4.
draft.remember: Modulus is the distance from the origin. Argument is the angle from the positive real axis.

a.q: What is the modulus of z = 3 − 4i?
a.why: |z| = √(3² + (−4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. Giving 25 is tempting, but that is the value before taking the square root.
a.clue: Use the distance formula from the origin, then take the root.

b.q: What is Arg z for z = −2i?
b.why: The point (0, −2) lies on the negative imaginary axis. Measured anticlockwise it is 3π/2, which is outside the range, so subtract 2π to get −π/2. The option π/2 is the positive imaginary axis.
b.clue: Which axis is the point on, and is the angle within −π to π?

problems.detail: The card says the argument is 'measured anticlockwise' but also allows negative values down to −π. It never says that negative arguments are measured clockwise, or how to bring an angle such as 3π/2 into the range. Question b depends on exactly this step, and only the why explains it.

proposal.title: Modulus and argument
card: A complex number z = a + bi is plotted on the Argand plane as the point (a, b). The horizontal axis is real and the vertical axis is imaginary.
|z| is the distance from the origin to the point. |z| = √(a² + b²).

Arg z is the angle from the positive real axis to the line joining the origin to the point, with −π < Arg z ≤ π. Anticlockwise angles are positive and clockwise angles are negative, and adding or subtracting 2π brings an angle into the range.
Example: z = 1 − √3i. |z| = √(1 + 3) = 2. The point is in the fourth quadrant. Measured anticlockwise the angle is 5π/3, which is too big, so Arg z = 5π/3 − 2π = −π/3.
proposal.remember: Modulus is the distance from the origin. Argument is the angle from the positive real axis, kept between −π and π.

a.q: What is the modulus of z = 3 − 4i?
a.why: |z| = √(3² + (−4)²) = √(9 + 16) = √25 = 5. Giving 25 is tempting, but that is the value before taking the square root.
a.clue: Use the distance formula from the origin, then take the root.

b.q: What is Arg z for z = −2i?
b.why: The point (0, −2) lies on the negative imaginary axis. Measured anticlockwise it is 3π/2, which is outside the range, so subtract 2π to get −π/2. That is the same as turning a quarter turn clockwise. The option π/2 is the positive imaginary axis.
b.clue: Which axis is the point on, and is the angle within −π to π?
